questions.takeaway: A database hosted on EC2 leaves the OS and engine upkeep with the customer, unlike a managed database.

read.text: Unmanaged, like EC2: AWS covers the physical layer, while each instance's OS, network setup and apps are yours to set up, secure and maintain.

questions.stem: An insurance broker installs and runs its own relational database engine on Amazon EC2 instances instead of using Amazon RDS. Which work does this choice add for the broker that Amazon RDS would have handled?

options.text: Patching the operating system and the database engine
options.why: On self-run EC2 the broker owns the OS and the engine installed on it, while RDS automates those patches.

options.text: Deciding which staff accounts may read the stored data
options.why: Who may read the data is the broker's choice with RDS as well, so this work is not added by EC2.

options.text: Maintaining the physical servers that host the database
options.why: AWS runs the hardware under EC2 just as it does under RDS, so the broker gains no hardware work.

options.text: Securing the data centers where the database runs
options.why: Physical security of the facilities is AWS's share whichever database option the broker picks.

questions.takeaway: Client-side encryption happens on the customer's own systems before data reaches AWS, unlike server-side encryption done by the service.

read.text: Client-side encryption: encrypting data on the client before the server gets it.

questions.stem: A hotel group protects the guest records it keeps on AWS in several ways. Which of these measures is client-side encryption?

options.text: Having the storage service encrypt the records after they arrive
options.why: Encryption done by the service after the records arrive is server-side encryption, whose owner varies by service.

options.text: Encrypting the records on its own servers before upload
options.why: Encrypting on the group's own systems before AWS receives the records is client-side encryption, a customer duty.

options.text: Limiting which staff accounts can open the records once stored
options.why: Controlling who can open the records is access control, which protects them without encrypting anything.

options.text: Applying vendor patches to the operating system on its servers
options.why: Patching the OS closes software flaws, but it does not encrypt the guest records at all.

questions.takeaway: Lambda bills by compute time and allocated memory, and memory also tunes the function's performance.

read.text: You pay for compute time only, per millisecond, priced by allocated memory.

questions.stem: Besides how long the code runs, which setting determines the price of an AWS Lambda function run?

options.text: The memory allocated to the function
options.why: Lambda prices each run's compute time by the memory the function is given.

options.text: The runtime the function's code uses
options.why: The runtime passes events to the code in its language, but it does not set the price of a run.

options.text: The event source that invokes it
options.why: The trigger decides when the function runs, while the price comes from run time and allocated memory.

options.text: The execution role it runs with
options.why: The execution role grants the function access to other services, and it plays no part in the bill.

questions.takeaway: Self-service Q&A and troubleshooting articles for AWS questions live in the AWS Knowledge Center.

read.text: Knowledge Center: Q&A, troubleshooting.

questions.stem: An admin at a garden center hits an error while setting up an AWS service and wants to search question-and-answer and troubleshooting articles before contacting anyone. Which resource fits?

options.why: Knowledge Center offers question-and-answer and troubleshooting articles the admin can search on their own.
Marketplace sells third-party software and services, not troubleshooting articles for AWS errors.
Trust and Safety Center takes reports of suspected AWS abuse and does not answer setup questions.
Trusted Advisor checks an account against best practices instead of answering a specific setup error.

questions.takeaway: A custom network ACL blocks all traffic until you add allow rules, unlike the default one that lets everything pass.

read.text: A custom network ACL starts the other way round: nothing passes until you add allow rules.

questions.stem: A video production studio creates a custom network ACL for a new subnet and associates it before writing any rules. What happens to traffic crossing that subnet's edge?

options.text: All of it is denied until allow rules are added
options.why: A new custom network ACL refuses everything, so the studio must add allow rules before any traffic passes.

options.text: All of it is allowed until deny rules are added
options.why: Allowing everything is how the default network ACL behaves, not a newly created custom one.

options.text: Inbound is denied while outbound is allowed
options.why: That split describes a security group's starting point, while a custom network ACL refuses both directions.

options.text: Replies to outbound requests pass in automatically
options.why: A network ACL is stateless and keeps no memory of requests, so replies get no automatic pass.

questions.takeaway: A steady, long-running workload earns the biggest discount by committing to its usage for a term.

read.text: Save when you commit: a usage commitment, usually 1 or 3 years, earns big discounts on steady workloads.

questions.stem: A payroll software firm runs the same compute load around the clock and expects it to stay steady for years. Which AWS pricing principle can lower its cost the most for this pattern?

options.why: A steady, predictable load is what a long usage commitment rewards with a large discount.
Paying as you go suits variable or uncertain demand, and gives no discount for a load that never changes.
Volume discounts follow how much the firm uses, while its steady load calls for a discount on a time commitment.
Reusing existing licenses is a licensing choice, rather than one of the AWS pricing principles for steady compute.

questions.takeaway: Launching EC2 instances in minutes removes the purchase, delivery and installation delays of physical servers.

read.text: Owning means upfront purchases, delivery waits, installation and fixed capacity.

questions.stem: A regional clinic plans to open a new patient portal next month. Its IT lead warns that physical servers would take weeks to arrive and be installed. Which benefit of running the portal on Amazon EC2 answers this concern most directly?

options.text: Speed of deployment, since instances can be running within minutes
options.why: Launching instances in minutes removes the delivery and installation wait the IT lead is worried about.

options.text: Global reach, since the portal can serve patients in other countries
options.why: Reaching other countries does not shorten the wait for servers before next month's opening.

options.text: High availability, since instances can run in several Availability Zones
options.why: Spreading instances across zones keeps the portal up, but the concern here is how long servers take to arrive.

options.text: Elasticity, since the portal's capacity can shrink during quiet nights
options.why: Shrinking capacity at night trims cost later, but it does nothing about the hardware delivery delay.

questions.takeaway: Buying hardware to a forecast risks idle excess or shortfalls, and scaling with actual demand is the stop guessing capacity benefit.

read.text: On premises you buy hardware for a forecast: plan for 10 million users over three years and get about 500,000, and the excess sits idle, while underestimating means a scramble for servers, degraded service and lost customers.

questions.stem: A school district bought servers sized for a projected surge in students that never came, and it still pays to power and maintain the idle hardware. On AWS, which approach would have kept it from paying for this unused capacity?

options.text: Paying lower unit prices because AWS buys its hardware in bulk
options.why: Bulk buying cuts the price of each server, but servers sized to a wrong forecast would still be paid for while idle.

options.text: Provisioning for current needs and scaling as usage changes
options.why: Sizing to present needs and scaling as usage changes avoids paying for capacity bought for a forecast that never came.

options.text: Running the district's portal from a Region in another country
options.why: A Region abroad changes where the portal runs, but the district would still pay for capacity it does not use.

options.text: Creating test environments for new ideas and deleting the failures
options.why: Throwaway test environments speed up experiments, but they do not size production capacity to real enrollment.

questions.takeaway: Managed services sit between unmanaged and serverless, with AWS running them and some setup left to the customer.

read.text: Managed: AWS absorbs much of the operational overhead, though some provisioning or configuration may remain yours depending on the service.

questions.stem: Which split of the work describes a managed service, such as Amazon SQS, as opposed to on-premises servers, unmanaged compute or fully managed compute?

options.text: AWS operates it day to day, and the customer handles some of its configuration
options.why: A managed service such as SQS lifts most of the operating work, yet some provisioning or configuration can stay with the customer.

options.text: AWS operates only its hardware, and the customer handles each instance's OS
options.why: Owning each instance's OS is the unmanaged EC2 split from the stem, which a managed service takes away.

options.text: AWS operates every server under it, and the customer handles just its code
options.why: Leaving only the code is the fully managed serverless split from the stem, while a managed service can still need setup.

options.text: AWS operates none of it, and the customer handles every layer of its own hardware
options.why: Running every layer in-house is the on-premises split from the stem, not a service that AWS runs day to day.

questions.takeaway: AWS Backup copies in other Regions survive a Regional outage, and organization-wide policies hold every account to one set of rules.

read.text: Cross-Region redundancy: copies in other Regions allow restores during a Regional outage.

questions.stem: A media company already uses AWS Backup, and its auditors set two new rules. Restores must still work if the company's main AWS Region goes offline, and every member account must follow one shared set of rules. Which AWS Backup capabilities meet these rules? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keeping copies of backups in a second Region
options.why: Copies held in another Region can still be restored when the main Region is offline, which meets the first rule.

options.text: Applying policies across a whole organization
options.why: Organization-wide policies put every member account under the same rules, which meets the second rule.

options.text: Showing jobs and restore points in one view
options.why: One view helps the team watch backups, but it neither survives a Region outage nor makes accounts follow rules.

options.text: Protecting new resources as soon as they appear
options.why: Auto-protection covers resources as they are created, but it does not keep restores working when a Region fails.

options.text: Encrypting backups and setting their schedules
options.why: Encryption and schedules protect each backup, but they meet neither the outage rule nor the shared-rules rule.

questions.takeaway: Region prices differ because each Region carries its own local operating, energy and tax costs.

read.text: AWS pricing is transparent and granular, yet each Region has its own rates.

questions.stem: Which statement explains why the same AWS service can carry a higher price in one Region than in another?

options.text: Each Region is walled off from every other AWS Region.
options.why: Isolation is true of every Region and protects data, but it is a security trait and does not set a service's price.

options.text: New features roll out to each Region at a different time.
options.why: Gradual rollout explains why a service may be missing in a Region, not why the same service costs more there.

options.text: Each Region has its own operating, energy and tax costs.
options.why: Each Region's rates reflect its local operating and energy costs, taxes and tax incentives, so prices vary by Region.

options.text: Edge locations cache content in places apart from Regions.
options.why: Edge locations do sit apart from Regions to cut latency, but where they sit does not set what a Region charges.

questions.takeaway: A queue between components loosely couples them, so one component's failure no longer cascades into the component that calls it.

read.text: Loosely coupled: a message queue sits between them, so A keeps sending while B is down and messages wait until B handles them.

questions.stem: An online florist's checkout service hands each order straight to its receipt service, so whenever the receipt service crashes, checkouts fail as well. The team places a message queue between the two services. What does this change give the florist?

options.text: Orders are held until the receipt service is able to take them
options.why: The queue keeps each order while the receipt service is down, so checkout keeps sending and no longer fails with it.

options.text: Receipt requests are spread across several healthy receipt instances
options.why: Spreading requests across healthy instances is what Elastic Load Balancing does, and a queue adds no such routing.

options.text: More receipt instances start up automatically as orders pile up
options.why: Starting instances as demand grows is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, which the florist did not add with the queue.

options.text: Buyers are sent a text message and an email when a receipt is ready
options.why: Texting and emailing buyers is a fan-out by Amazon SNS, while a queue only holds messages for a consumer to read.

questions.takeaway: Running every part of an application in the cloud, whether migrated or newly built, is a cloud-based deployment.

read.text: Cloud-based deployment: everything in the cloud, also called public cloud.

questions.stem: A new recipe-sharing website has no existing servers. It plans to build its application, database and networking entirely on AWS. Which deployment model is this?

options.why: Hybrid mixes in-house systems with cloud ones, but the website has no in-house systems at all.
On-premises keeps resources in the company's own facility, while the website puts everything on AWS.
Co-location places the company's own servers in a shared facility, while the website owns no servers.
Running every part of the application in the cloud, whether migrated or built new, is a cloud-based deployment.

questions.takeaway: Central management of SSL/TLS certificates for HTTPS points to AWS Certificate Manager.

read.text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): central management of SSL/TLS certificates for AWS services and connected on-premises resources.

questions.stem: An online language school serves its site over HTTPS from several AWS services and wants one place to handle the SSL/TLS credentials that let browsers trust those connections. Which service fits?

options.why: ACM centrally manages SSL/TLS certificates for AWS services, which is what these HTTPS connections rely on.
AWS KMS controls general-purpose encryption keys, not the certificates that secure HTTPS connections.
Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials like database passwords, not SSL/TLS certificates.
IAM Identity Center gives staff one login across accounts and has no role in serving certificates.

questions.takeaway: Finding sensitive data such as personal details inside S3 buckets points to Amazon Macie.

read.text: Amazon Macie: uses machine learning (ML) and automation to find and monitor sensitive data at rest in S3, aiding security posture reviews and compliance.

questions.stem: A recruitment agency stores uploaded resumes across many Amazon S3 buckets and needs to find which buckets hold personal data such as home addresses. Which service fits?

options.why: Macie uses machine learning to discover and monitor sensitive data stored in S3, such as personal details.
Inspector scans compute resources for software vulnerabilities, not S3 objects for personal data.
GuardDuty watches account and network activity for threats and does not classify what data buckets hold.
Security Hub gathers findings from other services into one view; it does not itself scan buckets for personal data.

questions.takeaway: For managed SFTP, FTPS or FTP transfers into Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS, choose AWS Transfer Family.

read.text: Fully managed file transfer in and out of Amazon S3 and Amazon EFS over FTP, SFTP, FTPS and other transfer protocols.

questions.stem: A payroll processor is migrating to AWS, including the on-premises SFTP and FTPS servers its partners use to send it files. After the migration, the files must land in Amazon S3 and no file servers may be left for the processor to manage. Which service fits?

options.why: Transfer Family runs fully managed SFTP and FTPS transfers into Amazon S3, so the processor runs no servers itself.
DataSync automates bulk moves from on-premises storage, rather than receiving partner files over SFTP or FTPS.
Direct Connect only supplies a private network line, with no managed SFTP or FTPS endpoint for partners.
The Snow Family ships data offline on devices, so it gives partners no SFTP or FTPS endpoint to send files to.

questions.takeaway: The AWS Health API gives programmatic access to Health events and needs AWS Premium Support.

read.text: AWS Health API: programmatic access.

questions.stem: Which option lets a company's in-house operations tool read AWS Health events in code instead of through the console?

options.why: The AWS Health API gives programmatic access to Health events, and it requires AWS Premium Support.
The dashboard is a console view for people, so it does not let the tool read events in code.
Trusted Advisor reports best-practice findings, and it is no programmatic source of AWS Health events.
CloudWatch dashboards display chosen metrics in the console and expose no AWS Health events to code.

questions.takeaway: Managed, scalable VPN access for individual remote workers is the job of AWS Client VPN.

read.text: For people: a fully managed, elastic VPN linking remote staff (and on-premises networks) to AWS that scales with demand.

questions.stem: Which AWS service gives individual remote employees managed VPN access to AWS that scales with demand and needs no hardware to run?

options.why: Client VPN is a fully managed, elastic VPN built for remote users, with no hardware to plan or operate.
Site-to-Site VPN links whole offices or data centers to a VPC, not individual employees.
Direct Connect is a dedicated physical line from a data center, not access for remote staff.
PrivateLink gives a VPC private access to services, not VPN access for people working remotely.

questions.takeaway: Policy-driven creation, retention and deletion of EBS snapshots is the job of Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager.

read.text: This fully managed service uses policies to create, keep and delete snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs on a schedule.

questions.stem: A film post-production studio has thousands of Amazon EBS volumes. It wants snapshots of them taken on a schedule, kept for a set time and then deleted, all driven by policies instead of manual work. Which service fits?

options.why: S3 Lifecycle moves objects between S3 storage classes, and it does not create or delete EBS snapshots.
EFS lifecycle management moves files between EFS classes, so it does nothing for EBS volumes.
Storage Gateway connects on-premises storage to AWS, and it does not run snapshot schedules for EBS.
Its policies create, keep and delete EBS snapshots on a schedule, which removes the manual work at scale.

questions.takeaway: Once identity is proven, authorization decides which actions and data that identity may reach.

read.text: Authorization then uses granted rights to limit that identity's actions.

questions.stem: A regional clinic must keep each patient's lab results private to meet its privacy duties. Once a patient has signed in, the portal shows only that patient's own results. Which core security concept does that second step apply?

options.why: Authentication already happened at sign-in; it proves who the patient is but sets no limit on what they open.
Authorization applies the rights granted to a known identity, so it keeps each patient to their own results.
Encryption in transit protects results while they cross the network, but it does not decide who may view them.
Auditing reviews records of past activity afterward, so it does not decide which results a patient may open now.

questions.takeaway: Securely connecting physical sensor devices to the cloud and acting on their data is the job of AWS IoT Core.

read.text: AWS IoT Core: managed service that securely links devices to cloud apps and simplifies ingesting, processing and acting on their data, using mutual authentication, end-to-end encryption and a choice of protocols.

questions.stem: Which AWS service securely connects sensor-equipped physical devices to cloud applications and helps ingest, process and act on the data they send?

options.why: EventBridge routes events between applications and services, but it is not built to connect and secure physical devices.
IoT Core links devices to cloud apps with mutual authentication and encryption and handles the data they send.
Kinesis Data Streams collects streaming records, but it does not authenticate and manage connections from devices.
AppSync builds GraphQL APIs for web and mobile frontends, not secure links for sensor devices.

questions.takeaway: Workforce single sign-on across AWS accounts with an existing corporate login points to IAM Identity Center.

read.text: Linked to an existing identity source, it gives staff one login for every connected account and service, which is SSO.

questions.stem: A university library wants staff to reach several AWS accounts with the corporate login they already use for email, instead of separate IAM users in each account. Which service fits?

options.why: IAM Identity Center links to the existing identity source and gives staff one login across connected accounts.
IAM is set up account by account, so it does not give staff one central login that reaches every connected account.
Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials for applications, not workforce sign-in across accounts.
Organizations groups and governs accounts but does not give staff single sign-on.

questions.takeaway: Choose Amazon EKS when a team wants Kubernetes on AWS with AWS operating the control plane.

read.text: With Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), AWS operates the Kubernetes control plane of each cluster for you.

questions.stem: A logistics company already runs its container workloads on open source Kubernetes in its own data center. It wants AWS to operate the Kubernetes control plane while its engineers keep their familiar Kubernetes tools. Which service fits?

options.why: EKS runs Kubernetes with AWS operating each cluster's control plane, so the engineers keep their tools.
ECS is AWS's own orchestrator rather than Kubernetes, so the familiar Kubernetes tools would not carry over.
ECR only stores container images, and it has no Kubernetes control plane to operate.
Elastic Beanstalk deploys apps from code and settings, and it does not run a Kubernetes control plane.

questions.takeaway: Managed near-real-time delivery of streaming data into storage or analytics tools points to Amazon Data Firehose.

read.text: Fully managed streaming ETL in near real time; provisions and scales itself; lands data in seconds in lakes, warehouses or analytics tools

questions.stem: Which AWS service is a fully managed way to capture streaming data and deliver it in near real time to data lakes, warehouses or analytics tools, scaling on its own?

options.why: Firehose is the managed streaming delivery service that lands data at its destination within seconds and scales itself.
Kinesis Data Streams captures data in real time for applications to read, but delivery to storage is not its role.
Glue runs managed ETL jobs on stored data and catalogs it, rather than capturing and delivering a stream.
Redshift is a data warehouse that can receive delivered data, not the service that carries the stream to it.

questions.takeaway: Suspected abuse coming from AWS resources is reported to the AWS Trust and Safety team.

read.text: Suspected misuse of AWS resources, such as odd network traffic coming from an AWS IP address, is reported to the AWS Trust and Safety team.

questions.stem: A university's IT team sees unusual network traffic reaching its servers from an AWS IP address and suspects that AWS resources are being misused. Where should the team report it?

options.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team
options.why: Suspected misuse of AWS resources, such as odd traffic from an AWS IP address, goes to the Trust and Safety team.
re:Post is for community questions, so a public post there is no way to report abuse to AWS.
A TAM serves a customer on its own plan, and the university is reporting someone else's resources.
Professional Services runs paid consulting projects, rather than taking reports of abuse.

questions.takeaway: A VPC endpoint for S3 gives a private path from the VPC to S3 and trims data transfer costs.

read.text: VPC endpoints connect a VPC privately to supported services, and one used for S3 trims transfer costs, notably out-of-Region.

questions.stem: A logistics company's application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in its own private network on AWS and moves large volumes of data to and from Amazon S3. The team wants a private path to S3 that also trims the data transfer charges on that path. What should it add?

options.why: A VPC endpoint links the network privately to S3, which keeps the traffic off the internet and trims transfer costs.
A NAT gateway sends traffic out toward the internet path, so it gives no private link to S3 and no transfer savings.
An internet gateway opens the network to the public internet, the opposite of the private path the team wants.
A Site-to-Site VPN links an on-premises network to AWS, rather than linking the company's AWS network to S3.

questions.takeaway: AWS Prescriptive Guidance is expert-written content covering migration, optimization and modernization, unlike peer forums or SDK guides.

read.text: AWS Prescriptive Guidance offers guides and patterns from AWS technology experts, with steps, architectures, tools and code for common migration, optimization and modernization work.

questions.stem: A seafood distributor wants its migration to AWS to carry less business risk, and its architects plan to build the migration strategy on AWS Prescriptive Guidance. Which statements about this resource are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Its material is written by AWS technology experts
options.why: The material comes from AWS technology experts, so the distributor builds its strategy on approaches AWS stands behind.

options.text: Its material also covers optimization and modernization work
options.why: Beyond the move itself, the guides and patterns cover optimizing and modernizing workloads, which helps after the migration too.

options.text: Its material is written by community peers who answer posted questions
options.why: Peers answering posted questions describes AWS re:Post, while Prescriptive Guidance is written by AWS technology experts.

options.text: Its material also covers the FAQ articles and videos of the AWS Knowledge Center
options.why: The Knowledge Center's FAQ articles and videos are hosted on AWS re:Post, not published as part of Prescriptive Guidance.

options.text: Its material is published as the SDK guides for calling AWS services
options.why: SDK guides are separate self-support documentation for developers, not the migration guides and patterns the architects plan to use.

questions.takeaway: A CloudWatch alarm acts when a metric crosses a threshold, such as texting staff through Amazon SNS.

read.text: Act when a metric crosses a threshold: notify, or change resources

questions.stem: An online pharmacy wants its on-call engineer to receive a text message whenever CPU use on its order servers rises above a chosen level. Which approach fits?

options.text: A CloudWatch alarm that sends a notice through Amazon SNS
options.why: An alarm fires when the CPU metric passes the chosen level and can text the engineer through Amazon SNS.

options.text: A CloudWatch dashboard that refreshes in near real time
options.why: A dashboard shows the CPU numbers on a screen, but it sends nothing to an engineer who is away from it.

options.text: CloudTrail Insights turned on for the account's trail
options.why: CloudTrail Insights flags unusual API activity, which is unrelated to how busy the order servers' CPUs are.

options.text: An AWS Config rule that checks each server's instance type
options.why: A Config rule judges resource settings against a policy, while the pharmacy needs a reaction to a live performance number.

questions.takeaway: With Amazon RDS, AWS handles patching, backups and hardware, while the customer still secures and encrypts the data.

read.text: AWS runs infrastructure, OS, patching and backups, while you own security measures and encryption at rest and in transit.

questions.stem: An online bookstore moves its order database from a server it ran itself to Amazon RDS for MySQL. An audit rule says the order records must be unreadable to anyone who copies the stored files or listens on the network. Under the shared responsibility model, who must set this up, and why?

options.text: AWS, since it runs the servers and operating system beneath RDS
options.why: AWS does run the layers beneath RDS, but making the order records unreadable to outsiders is not part of that upkeep.

options.text: The bookstore, since it picks when the automated backups run
options.why: The bookstore does choose the backup schedule, but that choice has nothing to do with keeping the records unreadable.

options.text: The bookstore, since data security stays with the customer
options.why: The audit rule calls for encryption at rest and in transit, and on RDS that kind of data protection stays with the bookstore.

options.text: AWS, since RDS applies the engine patches for the bookstore
options.why: RDS does take engine patching off the bookstore, but patching does not make the order records unreadable to outsiders.

questions.takeaway: Reviewed text templates that build matching resource stacks across accounts point to AWS CloudFormation.

read.text: Its templates are text files declaring what to build, not how, and it provisions and configures it all through AWS APIs.

questions.stem: A logistics company wants its network, servers and databases described in text files that reviewers approve before each release. The same files must then create matching environments in each of its AWS accounts. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Elastic Beanstalk deploys and runs an application for you, rather than building any set of resources from files the team writes.
AWS Config records and evaluates how existing resources are set up; it does not create them from a template.
CloudFormation reads declarative templates and provisions the resources they describe, giving matching environments in every account.
Systems Manager helps operate and patch resources that already exist, not build whole environments from reviewed templates.

questions.takeaway: A large migration runs through three phases in order, assess, mobilize, then migrate and modernize, and assess yields the business case.

read.text: Order: assess, mobilize, migrate and modernize.

questions.stem: A pet supply retailer follows the three-phase AWS process for a large migration to the cloud. Which activities belong to the first of the three phases? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Gauging how ready the organization is for the cloud
options.why: Gauging readiness is part of assess, the first phase, which checks how prepared the retailer is before anything else.

options.text: Writing the plan around the dependencies of each app
options.why: Writing the plan around app dependencies is the mobilize phase, the second of the three, so it comes after assess.

options.text: Setting the outcomes and goals the move has to reach
options.why: Setting outcomes and goals for the move is part of assess, the first phase, before any planning or moving starts.

options.text: Closing the readiness gaps across the organization
options.why: Closing readiness gaps is work for the mobilize phase, which follows assess and readies the organization for the move.

options.text: Weighing the findings into a business case for the move
options.why: Weighing findings into a business case, often with Migration Evaluator, is the output of assess, the first phase.

options.text: Picking one of the seven strategies for each app
options.why: Picking a strategy for each app is part of the mobilize phase, the second of the three, so it is not first-phase work.

questions.takeaway: A cloud contact center that routes, records and analyzes customer calls and chats is Amazon Connect.

read.text: Amazon Connect: AI-powered cloud contact center for calls and chats, with call routing, recording, analytics and AWS integrations.

questions.stem: Which AWS service provides a cloud contact center that routes customer calls and chats to agents and records the conversations?

options.why: Amazon SES sends email from applications, and it does not handle calls, chats or agent routing.
Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots, but it is not a full contact center that routes and records calls.
Amazon Connect is the cloud contact center, with routing of calls and chats, recording and analytics.
Amazon SNS pushes notifications to subscribers, which is not a service for agents to take customer calls.

questions.takeaway: A chat or voice bot that understands requests and talks back is built with Amazon Lex.

read.text: Lifelike voice or text chat via NLU and ASR (language understanding, speech recognition)

questions.stem: A regional bank wants a support assistant on its website that customers can type or speak to. The assistant must understand each request and reply in a back-and-forth conversation. Which AWS service should the bank use to build it?

options.why: Lex combines language understanding and speech recognition to build bots that hold a conversation by voice or text.
Polly can give a bot a speaking voice, but it does not understand what the customer asks or manage the dialog.
Transcribe writes down what was said, yet it cannot work out the request or answer the customer.
Comprehend finds sentiment and key phrases in text, but it does not run a conversation with the customer.

questions.takeaway: S3 Versioning keeps earlier versions of objects, so accidental deletes and overwrites can be undone.

read.text: Versioning lets you bring back earlier versions after an accidental delete.

questions.stem: A designer at a marketing agency deleted a client's logo from an Amazon S3 bucket by mistake. Which S3 feature, if switched on beforehand, lets the agency bring the logo back?

options.why: Lifecycle rules move or expire objects as they age, so they cannot restore an object someone deleted.
Block Public Access controls who may reach objects, and it keeps no earlier copies to restore.
Versioning keeps earlier versions of each object, so the deleted logo can be restored.
Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers to save cost, and it keeps no earlier copies.

questions.takeaway: Trusted Advisor's security checks flag gaps such as a root user without MFA and security groups open to the public.

read.text: Root user without MFA, security groups open to the public

questions.stem: Which AWS Trusted Advisor findings belong to the check category that guards against unauthorized access? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An EBS volume has no snapshot
options.why: A volume without a snapshot is a fault tolerance finding, since the risk is lost data rather than a security gap.

options.text: An RDS database instance sits idle
options.why: An idle database wastes money, so it is a cost optimization finding rather than a security one.

options.text: MFA is off for the root user
options.why: A root user without MFA is a security check, since that account holds the widest access of all.

options.text: EC2 instances all run in one Availability Zone
options.why: Instances crowded into one Availability Zone are a fault tolerance finding, since one zone failing could halt the app.

options.text: An EC2 instance is barely used
options.why: An underused instance is a cost optimization finding that points to scaling down, not to a gap in access control.

options.text: A security group allows traffic from anywhere
options.why: A security group that admits anyone exposes resources to attack, which is why it falls in the security category.

questions.takeaway: The Billing and Cost Management dashboard is the first stop to see charges and forecasts, get invoices and pay.

read.text: Monthly forecast, top services by cost, charges, usage, reports, invoices, payment methods

questions.stem: The treasurer of a community theater opens the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard for a first look at the account's spending. Which tasks does the dashboard itself handle, without another AWS tool? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Viewing the forecast for this month's spend
options.why: The dashboard shows a monthly forecast alongside current charges, usage and the top services by cost.

options.text: Downloading invoices and updating payment methods
options.why: Invoices and payment methods live in the dashboard, which is the treasurer's first stop for paying the bill.

options.text: Setting a custom budget for one service or tag
options.why: Custom budgets by service or tag are built in AWS Budgets, which the dashboard only links to.

options.text: Getting an alert when spend passes a set limit
options.why: Threshold alerts come only from AWS Budgets, so the dashboard alone does not warn the treasurer.

options.text: Estimating the cost of a design before deploying it
options.why: Estimating a planned design is what the AWS Pricing Calculator does, before any resources exist to bill.

questions.takeaway: A CloudWatch dashboard puts chosen metrics on one custom console page that refreshes itself.

read.text: Custom console pages, one view, near real time, self-refreshing

questions.stem: Which feature gives a team one customizable console page that shows its chosen CloudWatch metrics together and refreshes on its own?

options.why: A CloudWatch dashboard is a custom console page that gathers chosen metrics into one view and keeps itself up to date.
Alarms watch for a metric crossing a threshold and then act, rather than laying metrics out on one page.
CloudWatch Logs stores and searches log files, which is a different job from showing metrics on one page.
The AWS Health Dashboard shows AWS events affecting an account, not a page of metrics the team picked itself.

questions.takeaway: Fixed-column tables that one query can join across point to a relational database.

read.text: Tables of rows and columns follow a rigid schema and share attributes, so one query spans customers and orders.

questions.stem: A bike rental shop keeps customers, bikes and rentals in separate tables where every row has the same fixed columns. Staff run one query that joins the tables to list each customer's past rentals. Which type of database fits this design?

options.why: Related tables under a fixed schema, joined by one query, are the defining traits of a relational database.
A key-value database uses a flexible schema and does not join related tables in one query.
A graph database stores nodes and their connections rather than tables of rows with fixed columns.
A cache only holds copies of hot data in RAM and is not the lasting home for the shop's records.

questions.takeaway: A unit price that falls as usage grows, with no commitment signed, is the pay less by using more principle.

read.text: Pay less by using more: economies of scale lower the unit price as usage grows, and some services use tiered pricing.

questions.stem: An online video course provider keeps adding data to Amazon S3, and its price per gigabyte drops as the total grows, even though it has signed no commitment. Which pricing principle explains the lower unit price?

options.why: The unit price falls with volume through tiered pricing, which needs no commitment, only growing usage.
Commitment discounts need a usage promise over a term, and the provider has signed none.
Paying as you go explains paying only for use, but by itself it does not lower the price of each extra gigabyte.
Reusing licenses affects software costs, while the falling storage rate here comes from volume.

questions.takeaway: AWS Artifact is the free, on-demand source for AWS compliance reports and for agreements with AWS.

read.text: A free portal that hands you AWS's own audit reports whenever needed and lets you handle certain online agreements.

questions.stem: Which AWS service is a no-cost portal for downloading AWS compliance reports on demand and for managing certain agreements with AWS?

options.why: Artifact is the free portal that supplies AWS's own audit reports and handles agreements between a customer and AWS.
Audit Manager gathers evidence about a customer's own controls, rather than handing out AWS's reports and agreements.
Config evaluates the settings of a customer's resources against rules and holds no AWS reports or agreements.
Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment, which has nothing to do with AWS's audit reports.

questions.takeaway: AWS Enterprise Support pairs a response in under 15 minutes for down critical systems with a designated TAM.

read.text: With Enterprise Support, a business-critical or mission-critical system that is down gets a response in under 15 minutes.

questions.stem: A stock trading platform needs a response in under 15 minutes when a mission-critical system is down, along with a designated technical account manager. It has no need for 24/7 workload monitoring by AWS. Which Support plan fits?

options.why: Enterprise Support answers a down mission-critical system in under 15 minutes and includes a designated TAM.
Business Support+ responds to a down critical system in under 30 minutes and has no designated TAM.
Unified Operations adds round-the-clock workload monitoring, which the platform said it has no need for.
Basic Support offers no technical support cases at all, let alone a fast response or a TAM.

questions.takeaway: A DDoS attack floods an app from many compromised machines until real users get no response.

read.text: A denial of service (DoS) attack exhausts an app's capacity so real customers get no answer.

questions.stem: A photography studio's booking site stops answering customers while a huge number of unknown home computers send requests straight to it. Which statements describe what is happening? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The traffic uses up the capacity real visitors need
options.why: The flood exhausts the site's capacity, so genuine customers get no answer while the attack lasts.

options.text: The sending computers are infected bots
options.why: Many unknown home computers taking part points to infected machines whose owners have no idea they are attacking.

options.text: A single attacker's machine sends all the traffic
options.why: Traffic from one machine is a plain DoS attack, while here a huge number of computers take part.

options.text: Forged requests make a public service reply to the site
options.why: Getting a public service to answer forged requests is a UDP flood, yet here the home computers contact the site directly.

options.text: Small requests are turned into much larger replies
options.why: Turning small requests into big replies happens through a public service in a UDP flood, not in requests sent straight to the site.

questions.takeaway: On-demand delivery means IT resources arrive within seconds of a request, with no hardware buying cycle.

read.text: On-demand delivery: resources within seconds, whenever needed.

questions.stem: An online bookstore needs extra storage for a holiday promotion. It wants the storage ready within seconds of asking, with no hardware order to place or wait for. Which characteristic of cloud computing does this rely on?

options.why: Getting resources within seconds, whenever they are asked for, is exactly what on-demand delivery provides.
Economies of scale lower prices through bulk buying, which says nothing about how fast storage arrives.
Fault tolerance keeps a system running through failures, which is unrelated to getting storage quickly.
Co-location means placing your own servers in a shared facility, which still needs a hardware order.

questions.takeaway: The mobilize phase readies the organization and produces the migration plan, built around application dependencies.

read.text: Mobilize: ready the organization and resources, write the plan around app dependencies, close readiness gaps and pick strategies (Application Discovery Service, Migration Hub).

questions.stem: A regional hospital has an approved business case for moving to AWS. In the mobilize phase, its team now readies staff and resources and closes readiness gaps. What should this phase produce?

options.text: A migration plan based on app dependencies
options.why: The mobilize phase writes the migration plan around application dependencies, after assess has produced the business case.

options.text: A business case from readiness findings
options.why: The business case comes out of the assess phase, which the hospital has already finished.

options.text: Applications moved and validated on AWS
options.why: Moving and validating applications happens in migrate and modernize, the phase after mobilize.

options.text: Replicated copies of every production database
options.why: Replicating production databases is part of the move itself, which belongs to migrate and modernize.

questions.takeaway: Lightsail is the simple, predictably priced choice for a small site or blog.

read.text: A cost-effective bundle: virtual private servers (VPSs) plus storage, databases and networking, for a predictable monthly price.

questions.stem: A family-owned florist wants to host a small marketing site and blog for a predictable monthly price, without learning the full AWS Management Console. Which service fits?

options.why: Lightsail bundles a virtual private server with storage and networking at a set monthly price, with no need for the full console.
Raw EC2 leaves the florist to choose and size each resource in the full console, with bills that vary by use.
Elastic Beanstalk builds and scales EC2 resources that bill by use, so the florist gets no set monthly price.
Outposts places AWS hardware in a customer's own data center, which gives neither a set small-site price nor a simpler console.

questions.takeaway: CloudTrail Insights learns normal API volume and error rates and flags activity that departs from them.

read.text: Studies management events for normal API volume and error rates, and flags deviations once enabled on a trail or event data store

questions.stem: A weather data startup wants AWS to learn the usual volume and error rate of API calls in its account and to flag any sudden departure from that pattern. Which feature fits?

options.why: Insights studies normal API volume and error rates and flags deviations, which is the pattern detection the startup wants.
Event history lists past management events for searching, but it does not learn a baseline or flag unusual activity.
Integrity validation shows whether log files were tampered with, which says nothing about unusual API volume.
Config rules judge resource settings against a standard, rather than watching the rate of API calls for odd spikes.

questions.takeaway: Standard SQL on data that stays in Amazon S3, with no warehouse to load, points to Amazon Athena.

read.text: 7 Perform data analytics: data scientists query S3 in place with standard SQL in Amazon Athena, which reads the catalog table to recognize the structure.

questions.stem: A marketing agency keeps its campaign logs in an Amazon S3 data lake. Its analysts want to run standard SQL queries on the logs where they already sit, without loading them into a warehouse first. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Athena runs standard SQL directly against data in S3, using catalog metadata to understand its structure.
Redshift is a data warehouse, so it suits heavy, frequent SQL on data loaded into it rather than querying S3 in place.
EMR runs big data frameworks on managed clusters, which is more than the analysts need for SQL on S3 data.
Quick Sight builds dashboards and reports for business users, and it is not a SQL query engine over S3.

questions.takeaway: Moving from a monolith to microservices contains a fault in one part, so the rest of the application keeps working.

read.text: A traditional monolith tightly couples its database logic, web servers, user interface and business logic, so one failure can take down the whole application.

questions.stem: A recipe website runs as one monolithic application, and last week a fault in its comment feature took the whole site offline, even though search and recipe pages never use comments. The team is now rebuilding the site as microservices. Which benefit of this move addresses that incident?

options.text: Each part can crash while the other parts keep serving
options.why: Microservices loosely couple the site's parts, so a comment fault stays contained while search and recipes keep working.

options.text: Each part can scale on its own as its own load changes
options.why: Scaling parts separately is a real gain of microservices, but it would not have kept the site up during the comment fault.

options.text: Each part can be updated without redeploying the rest
options.why: Shipping one part's changes alone adds flexibility, but it does nothing to stop a comment fault from spreading to search.

options.text: Each part can use the language and tools that suit it
options.why: Choosing tools per part is a flexibility gain, but the incident came from one fault taking down the whole site.

questions.takeaway: MFA requires at least two kinds of proof, such as a password plus a one-time code.

read.text: MFA requires at least two kinds of proof, such as the password plus a one-time code from a phone app.

questions.stem: Which access control requires a user to present a password plus a one-time code from a phone app at sign-in?

options.why: MFA asks for two or more kinds of proof, such as a password plus a one-time code from a phone app.
A password policy sets rules such as minimum length for IAM user passwords, yet it still asks for one kind of proof.
Single sign-on gives one login for many connected accounts, which reduces logins rather than adding a second proof.
Assuming a role grants temporary permissions and does not by itself make the user present a one-time code.

questions.takeaway: ELB is a Regional service that gives a tier one entry point to the instances behind it.

read.text: ELB is Regional, so front ends need only its single URL, and it passes each request to the back-end instance with the fewest outstanding requests.

questions.stem: At what scope does Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) operate when it gives front-end instances a single address to send their requests to?

options.why: ELB is a Regional service, so one entry point serves instances across the Region.
ELB is not limited to a single zone, which would make that zone a single point of failure.
Edge locations serve content delivery, while ELB runs within a Region in front of its instances.
ELB is not tied to one subnet, since it spreads traffic over instances across the Region.

questions.takeaway: User data runs a script at launch to configure an instance, such as installing software its AMI lacks.

read.text: User data: a launch script, here installing and starting Nginx, which the generic AMI lacks.

questions.stem: A car dealership launches instances from a generic Linux AMI that has no web server installed. It wants each instance to install and start a web server on its own when it first boots. Which launch setting does this?

options.why: User data runs a script at launch, so it can install and start the web server on each new instance.
A key pair controls who can log in, and it does not run any setup steps at launch.
The instance type sets CPU, memory and network performance, not the software installed at boot.
Network settings decide which traffic can reach the instance, not what software it installs.

questions.takeaway: Compliance means meeting every regulation, industry standard and internal policy that applies to a workload's data.

read.text: It is a security and data-protection bar: your resources and data must satisfy each internal policy, industry standard and regulation that binds you.

questions.stem: An online fashion retailer stores personal data about shoppers in the European Union, so GDPR applies to it. Which statement describes what compliance means for the retailer?

options.text: Its data must satisfy every rule that binds the retailer
options.why: Compliance is the bar of meeting every law, industry standard and internal policy that applies, with GDPR as one of them here.

options.text: Its traffic must be watched nonstop for unusual behavior
options.why: Constant watching for anomalies is monitoring, which supports compliance but does not by itself mean meeting GDPR.

options.text: Its controls must be reviewed now and then to see they work
options.why: A periodic review of controls is auditing, a check along the way rather than the bar of meeting the rules itself.

options.text: Its records must be shielded from any unauthorized access
options.why: Stopping unauthorized access is the securing step, a foundation for compliance rather than a definition of it.

questions.takeaway: When nobody knows which servers an app depends on, AWS Application Discovery Service builds the inventory for the plan.

read.text: Nobody knows which servers an app relies on: AWS Application Discovery Service.

questions.stem: The IT team at an engineering firm is unsure which servers and databases its order system relies on. Before planning the move, it wants an automatic inventory of its on-premises servers and the connections between them. Which service fits?

options.why: Application Discovery Service automatically inventories on-premises servers, databases and links, which feeds the migration plan.
Migration Hub is the central view for tracking migration tasks, while the inventory itself comes from Application Discovery Service.
Migration Evaluator builds the cost-backed business case, rather than an inventory of server dependencies.
Application Migration Service moves the applications once the plan exists, so it comes after the inventory.

questions.takeaway: In AWS Organizations, accounts with shared compliance or security needs are grouped into an organizational unit.

read.text: Grouping: OUs gather accounts by security, compliance or budget needs, such as a developer OU.

questions.stem: A biotech company runs many AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The accounts that hold lab research data all share the same regulatory needs, and the company wants to manage those accounts together, so a policy set once reaches each of them. What should it do?

options.text: Place the lab accounts in one organizational unit
options.why: An OU gathers accounts with the same compliance needs so policies applied to it reach every account inside.

options.text: Turn on consolidated billing for the organization
options.why: Consolidated billing rolls every account's charges into one bill, but it sets apart no group of lab accounts for policies.

options.text: Create an IAM group for researchers in each account
options.why: An IAM group gathers users inside one account, so it groups people rather than the lab accounts themselves.

options.text: Turn on AWS CloudTrail in every lab account
options.why: CloudTrail records the API calls made in each account, which audits activity but groups no accounts for policies.

questions.takeaway: AWS DMS migrates databases while the source stays live and can keep replicating changes so source and target stay in sync.

read.text: You name the source and target, and a scheduled task on a replication VM copies the data while the source stays live.

questions.stem: A concert ticketing platform will move its production database to AWS with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Ticket sales must go on while the migration runs, and the target must pick up every sale made until the cutover. Which AWS DMS capabilities meet these two needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It moves the data while the source database stays live
options.why: AWS DMS moves data with a scheduled task while the source stays live, so ticket sales go on during the migration.

options.text: It keeps applying ongoing source changes to the target
options.why: With replication, AWS DMS goes past a one-time copy and keeps the target in sync with each new sale until cutover.

options.text: It also moves NoSQL databases and data warehouses
options.why: This is true of AWS DMS, but the range of database types it supports does nothing to keep sales running or the copy current.

options.text: It handles moves to the same engine or to a new one
options.why: This is true of AWS DMS, but support for both migration types is about engines rather than the platform's uptime or new sales.

options.text: It can carry terabytes of data at a low cost
options.why: This is true of AWS DMS, but a low price for large moves meets neither the need for live sales nor the need to capture new ones.

questions.takeaway: AWS security controls serve three goals: prevent incidents, protect resources, and detect and respond to incidents.

read.text: Controls prevent incidents by access management, protect networks, apps and data, and detect and respond to incidents.

questions.stem: AWS groups its security controls by the goal each one serves. Which set names those goals?

options.text: Prevent, protect, and detect and respond
options.why: The controls stop incidents through access management, shield networks, apps and data, and catch and handle incidents that occur.

options.text: Plan, build, and test and deploy
options.why: These are stages of shipping software, which describe a delivery process rather than the aims of security controls.

options.text: Encrypt, archive, and back up and restore
options.why: Encryption and backups are individual protections, so this list mixes tools with tasks instead of naming control goals.

options.text: Monitor, alert, and scale and recover
options.why: Monitoring and scaling are operational tasks for health and capacity, not the goals AWS sets for its security controls.

questions.takeaway: Instance store gives very fast, free disk for temporary data such as caches and scratch space that can be lost.

read.text: Being ephemeral, it suits data you can lose, such as buffers, caches and scratch space for heavy processing.

questions.stem: A weather research lab runs heavy simulations on one Amazon EC2 instance and writes scratch files it can lose without harm. It wants the fastest disk the instance can reach, at no extra cost. Which statements explain the best storage choice for those scratch files? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Amazon EBS keeps a volume's data through instance stops
options.why: EBS persistence is true but wasted here, since the scratch files can be lost and EBS volumes are billed on top of the instance.

options.text: EC2 instance store sits on the host, so latency is very low
options.why: Disk on the instance's own host gives the lowest latency and highest I/O, which is the speed the lab wants.

options.text: Amazon EFS lets many instances share one file system
options.why: EFS sharing is true but not needed for one instance, and a local instance store disk is usually faster than EFS.

options.text: EC2 instance store comes free with many instance types
options.why: Instance store is included with many instance types at no extra cost, which meets the lab's cost goal.

options.text: Amazon EBS volumes change size and type without downtime
options.why: Live EBS changes are true but beside the point, because the lab needs neither resizing nor persistence for scratch data.

options.text: Amazon EFS grows and shrinks as files are added or removed
options.why: EFS elasticity is true but does not make it the fastest or a free disk, so it does not meet the lab's goals.

questions.takeaway: Private access from a VPC to one chosen service, as if it were local, is the job of AWS PrivateLink.

read.text: For resources: highly available, scalable private access from a VPC to services as if they were inside it, including other VPCs, other clouds and on-premises networks.

questions.stem: Which AWS service lets a VPC reach one specific service in another VPC as if that service were local, without a public IP address or an internet gateway?

options.why: PrivateLink exposes only the chosen service to the VPC over a private path, with no public IP or internet gateway.
Transit Gateway joins whole networks through a hub rather than exposing one service as if it were local.
Direct Connect is a dedicated line from a data center to AWS, not private access between VPC services.
Client VPN gives remote people access to AWS, not one VPC private access to a service in another.

questions.takeaway: Moving to a managed service such as Amazon RDS with no new code is replatforming, a lift, tinker and shift.

read.text: MySQL to Amazon RDS with no code changes: replatform.

questions.stem: An online florist moves its self-managed MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL so that AWS handles more of the upkeep. It writes no new code and keeps the same architecture. Which migration strategy is this?

options.why: Replatforming makes a few cloud optimizations, such as moving MySQL to Amazon RDS, without new code or architecture changes.
Rehost moves an application exactly as it is, while the florist gains a managed database service along the way.
Refactor writes new code and cloud-built features, which the florist avoids here.
Repurchase swaps licensed software for a SaaS product, while the florist keeps MySQL.

questions.takeaway: A benefit of the AWS Cloud is using data centers with redundant power, cooling and security without owning or maintaining them.

read.text: Data center: a server building with redundant power, cooling and security.

questions.stem: A small engineering startup needs its servers in a building with redundant power, cooling and security. It has no staff to build such a facility or keep it running. How does the AWS Cloud meet this need?

options.text: It lets the startup cache copies of popular content at sites close to its users
options.why: Edge locations speed up delivery to users, but they give the startup no facility to house its servers.

options.text: It lets the startup pick the geographic area where its customers are concentrated
options.why: Choosing a Region near customers cuts delay, but on its own it says nothing about who runs the facility.

options.text: It lets the startup use AWS data centers that it neither owns nor maintains
options.why: AWS runs the server buildings with their power, cooling and security, so the startup uses them without upkeep.

options.text: It lets the startup define a private virtual network inside its own account
options.why: A virtual network organizes resources in software, but it does not supply or run the physical facility.

questions.takeaway: Amazon ECR is the registry that holds container images for ECS or EKS to pull.

read.text: A fully managed registry to keep, manage and deploy images, stored securely in repositories.

questions.stem: Which AWS service stores container images in secure repositories, so that container orchestrators can pull them when they deploy?

options.why: ECR is the managed image registry that orchestrators pull container images from.
EFS is a shared file system for instances, not a registry built for container images.
Fargate is the serverless compute that containers run on, and it does not keep image repositories.
EKS orchestrates containers with Kubernetes, and it pulls images from a registry rather than storing them.

questions.takeaway: Lasting, conditional access to a bucket for another AWS account is written as a resource-based S3 bucket policy.

read.text: Bucket policies are JSON documents controlling who may reach the objects inside.

questions.stem: A regional clinic wants a partner laboratory's AWS account to upload test results into Amazon S3 storage that the clinic owns, on an ongoing basis. A condition must keep the clinic in full control of every uploaded object. What should the clinic use?

options.text: An identity-based policy on the clinic's IAM users
options.why: A policy on the clinic's own users only sets what those users may do, so it grants nothing to identities in the laboratory's account.
A bucket policy can name the partner account as principal, allow uploads and add a condition on object ownership.

options.text: A presigned URL for each upload
options.why: A presigned URL expires, so it suits brief one-off access rather than lasting uploads from a partner account.
Block Public Access only stops public access, so it grants nothing to the partner laboratory.

questions.takeaway: In the cloud computing definition, over the internet means resources are used remotely through web services rather than local hardware.

read.text: Cloud computing: IT resources, on demand, over the internet, billed pay-as-you-go.

questions.stem: A city library's staff open its catalog servers and file storage from any branch, or from home, through a web browser, with no equipment kept in each building. Which part of the AWS definition of cloud computing does this way of reaching the resources reflect?

options.why: On-demand delivery is about getting resources within seconds, while the library's need is reaching them from any place.
IT resources names what is delivered, such as servers and storage, rather than the way staff reach them.
Using servers and storage remotely through web-based access, from any location, is the over the internet part.
Pay-as-you-go pricing covers how the library is billed, which says nothing about how staff reach the resources.

questions.takeaway: To survive one Availability Zone failing without paying for a second Region, run across several AZs in the same Region.

read.text: Multi-AZ covers one AZ failing: the app moves to a backup AZ you set up, with quicker disaster recovery, continuity, lower latency and compliance as bonuses.

questions.stem: A regional clinic runs its appointment booking app in one AWS Region. The app must keep working if one isolated location in that Region fails, but leadership accepts the risk of a full Region outage to hold down cost. Which design fits?

options.text: Copy it into a second AWS Region
options.why: A second Region guards against a whole Region failing, a risk the clinic chose to accept, so it adds cost beyond the need.

options.text: Spread it across several AZs in the Region
options.why: Running in more than one Availability Zone lets the app fail over to a backup AZ when one location goes down.

options.text: Serve it from Amazon CloudFront edge locations
options.why: Edge locations cache content near users and are not where the booking app and its data run.

options.text: Move it to one larger EC2 instance
options.why: One bigger instance still sits in a single location, so that location failing takes the app down.

questions.takeaway: Replacing licensed software with a SaaS product, often from a new vendor, is the repurchase strategy.

read.text: Repurchase trades licensed software for SaaS, often from a new vendor.

questions.stem: A property management company drops the licensed customer relationship management software it runs itself. It moves its sales team to a SaaS product from a different vendor. Which migration strategy is this?

options.why: Repurchase, or drop and shop, swaps a traditional license for SaaS, often from a new vendor, as the company does here.
Replatform keeps the same application and adds a few cloud optimizations, while this company changes products entirely.
Rehost moves the same application to AWS unchanged, while the company replaces it with another vendor's product.
Retire switches an application off with nothing in its place, while the sales team still needs its software.
